item.description: Prokinetic agents are used to enhance upper gastrointestinal motility, but adverse events related to these agents are poorly described. item.title: Swedish Consensus Recommendation for Follow-Up After ICU Stay.
item.description: A substantial proportion of intensive care unit (ICU) survivors experience long-term physical, psychological and cognitive impairments after critical illness. item.title: Management of Patients After Cardiac Arrest.
item.description: Cardiac arrest remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality, although contemporary care now enables potential survival with good neurologic outcome. The core acute management goals for survivors of cardiac arrest are to provide organ support, sustain adequate hemodynamics, and evaluate the underlying cause of the cardiac arrest. item.description: Several parsimonious scores predict acute kidney injury (AKI), but their comparative performance in critically ill adults is uncertain. item.title: Causal mediation analysis of contact with COVID-19 patients and burnout syndrome in physiotherapists in Japan: secondary analysis of a multicentre observational study.
item.description: This study looked at Japanese physiotherapists who worked with COVID-19 patients and found that direct contact with patients contributed to burnout, but this effect was partly buffered by appreciation and respect from patients and colleagues. The study suggests that organisational resources, such as reimbursement for care, may also play a role in burnout. Burnout prevalence was 19.4% among the physiotherapists.

item.title: Bedside pharmacist interventions for managing intravenous drug incompatibilities in critically ill patients.
item.description: Patients admitted to intensive care units are at increased risk of intravenous drug incompatibilities, owing to polypharmacy and the limited number of available venous access devices. To evaluate bedside pharmacist interventions for managing drug incompatibilities identified during intravenous administration in intensive care unit patients. A cross-sectional study with prospective data collection was conducted between June and December 2025 in five intensive care units of a university hospital.

item.description: Fluid administered after norepinephrine initiation may reflect both resuscitation decisions and evolving illness severity, making observational comparisons susceptible to confounding and reverse causation. To evaluate associations between fluid volume during the first 6 h after norepinephrine initiation and mortality and incident invasive ventilation. item.description: Hospital-acquired anemia (HAA), which negatively affects morbidity, mortality, and resource use, is a common iatrogenic effect of hospitalization, especially in intensive care units. Contributing factors include phlebotomy, intravenous fluid resuscitation, and medications. item.title: Serial plasma proenkephalin A 119-159 and dipeptidyl peptidase 3 after cardiac arrest: association with long-term neurological outcome.
item.description: To evaluate whether serial plasma proenkephalin A 119-159 (penKid) and circulating dipeptidyl peptidase 3 (cDPP3) after cardiac arrest are associated with long-term neurological outcome and mortality. We performed a retrospective multicentre cohort study of adults admitted to intensive care after cardiac arrest in southern Sweden. Biomarkers were measured on admission and at 12 and 48 h. item.description: Hypoxic ischemic brain injury (HIBI) remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality in patients following cardiac arrest. Many international guidelines for HIBI prognostication advocate for a multimodal approach with inclusion of blood-based biomarkers. item.title: Association between destination hospital level and outcomes in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest patients under a dispatch-guided transport system: a population-based study in Nagoya, Japan.
item.description: The relationship between destination hospital level and outcomes in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients remains controversial. item.description: Medical television dramas shape public perceptions of cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). The Pitt has been praised for its clinical realism but has not been systematically evaluated. We assessed adherence of televised CPR to current European Resuscitation Council (ERC) and American Heart Association (AHA) guidelines. item.description: Hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury is the leading cause of death and long-term disability after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and is driven by the ischaemia-reperfusion syndrome, for which no specific treatment exists. Remote ischaemic post-conditioning (brief, repeated cycles of limb ischaemia and reperfusion delivered with a pneumatic cuff), is protective across ischemia-reperfusion conditions. item.title: The Relationship Between Caring Roles and Fatigue in Intensive Care Nurses: A Cross-Sectional Study.
item.description: Intensive care nurses experience significant levels of fatigue while providing care to their patients. High levels of fatigue may negatively impact nurses' orientation to their caring roles, and this orientation may also be a cause of fatigue. item.description: Coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS) have emerged as significant pathogens in bloodstream infections (BSIs). Currently, no validated models exist for specifically predicting in-hospital mortality in patients with CoNS-BSIs. A retrospective study was conducted on adult patients with CoNS-BSIs using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-III) database. item.description: As Intensive Care Unit (ICU) survival improves, attention has shifted towards patients' psychological well-being and recovery. Although Virtual Reality (VR) is increasingly used in critical care, patients' experiences of VR interventions have not been comprehensively synthesised. item.title: Management of Intensive Care Unit Admission of Patients With Blood Cancer.
item.description: Patients with blood cancer are at high risk of complications requiring intensive care. Admission to the intensive care unit (ICU) involves ethical and organizational complexities. To investigate the perspectives of hematologists and intensivists making ICU admission decisions in France. item.description: High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) therapy is often used in critical care, but its effects on swallowing function remain unclear. item.description: Sleep deprivation and poor sleep quality are critical problems among intensive care unit (ICU) patients, with significant implications for recovery, delirium onset and clinical outcomes. item.description: Postoperative delirium is a serious complication in intensive care units (ICUs), particularly following cardiac surgery. item.description: Despite established guidelines, central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) remains a severe ICU complication due to cognitive and resource barriers hindering healthcare worker compliance. item.description: The transition from the intensive care unit (ICU) to a general ward is a period of heightened vulnerability, yet the precise timing and modifiable predictors of adverse events remain poorly defined. item.description: Intensive care unit (ICU) nurses are exposed to numerous alarms, many of which are unnecessary and lead to alarm fatigue. item.description: The integration of AI and robotic systems into critical care necessitates examining how ICU nurses preserve clinical judgement, professional accountability and person-centred care while using these technologies. item.description: Effective communication during family conferences (FC) in the intensive care unit (ICU) is essential for supporting families and fostering trust. item.description: Patient and public involvement (PPI) is increasingly recommended in health research to enhance relevance, quality and implementation of findings. item.description: Maintaining privacy in intensive care units (ICUs) is challenging because of high workload, invasive procedures, continuous monitoring and shared care environments. item.description: Research priorities for intensive care nursing have been set internationally but not in Japan. We aimed to identify national priorities and compare them with those reported elsewhere. item.description: When engaged in experiential learning, trainees enter a complex ecosystem where expertise relies on collaboration and the intentional use of environmental resources. item.description: Anticipatory grief and Post-Intensive Care Syndrome-Family (PICS-F) are increasingly recognised as important sources of psychological distress among family members of critically ill patients. item.description: Building rapport, understood as establishing a meaningful and trusting relationship through interpersonal interactions between healthcare professionals and patients or their family members, was described in research as early as the 1960s. item.description: Family members often assume caregiving responsibilities after a patient's discharge from the intensive care unit (ICU). Many family members are inadequately prepared due to limited training and support. item.description: Podcasts have emerged as prominent tools for asynchronous medical education, widely adopted across training levels and specialties. item.description: The management of critically ill patients with opioid use disorder presents a unique challenge, as overdose, withdrawal, or concomitant intoxication, due to an unregulated drug supply, leads to physiologic changes that potentially impact standard treatment. item.description: Linezolid is important for treating infections caused by Gram-positive bacteria resistant to first-line agents.
